newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage backeds unchanged to slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage backeds unchanged to slightly lower.

text.p: Activity in the U.S. mortgage-backed securities market slowed on Thursday, with prices just above opening levels, traders said.
At 1500 EST/1900 GMT, mortgages were mostly up 1/32. Higher coupons were unchanged.
Yield spreads over Treasuries generally held steady.
The dollar roll plays that abounded on Wednesday were hardly seen on Thursday, market experts said.
"The Ginnie 8.0 roll is trading cheap and the Ginnie 8.5 is looking attractive, but other than that the rolls aren't really trading," one trader said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 1/32 at 100-13/32, yielding 106 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 1/32 as well, at 100-08/32 and 100-13/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was unchanged at 100-07/32 to yield 6.47 percent.
Both mortgages and Treasuries appeared to be treading water, waiting for Friday's report on January employment, analysts said.
